title: Could Garrett Crochet return to Red Sox in a bullpen role?
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Garrett Crochet, recovering from injuries, may return to Red Sox in a bullpen role for 2026.
Crochet has been sidelined since April due to shoulder inflammation and a lat strain.
Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy indicated Crochet may not return as a starter this season.

title: Lost a python? Boston Animal Care and Control might have it.
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: A ball python was found near Ellington Street in Dorchester and is now in custody with Boston Animal Care and Control.
The python, temporarily named 'Tippy,' was left in a cage near a community garden before being reported by locals.
Officials urge anyone with information about the python to contact Boston Animal Care and Control at 617-635-1800.

title: Tommy DeVito bests Drake Maye, and other takeaways from Patriots’ training camp scrimmage
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Team Blue, led by Tommy DeVito, defeated Team White 22-15 in the Patriots training camp scrimmage.
DeMario Douglas stood out for Team Blue with six catches and two touchdowns, including a 50-yard play.
Several players, including Will Campbell and Carlton Davis, missed the scrimmage due to injuries and personal reasons.

title: A closer look at Harwich, voted the best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich voted best town on Cape Cod by over 850 Boston.com readers in an informal poll.
Harwich features 11 miles of shoreline, seven villages, and over 20 beaches on the Lower Cape.
Notable spots in Harwich include Saquatucket Marina, The Port Restaurant & Bar, and Cape Cod Lavender Farm.

title: DA’s office says prosecutor’s ‘hot mic’ moment in Lindsay Clancy trial was misheard
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Plymouth DA's office claims 'shut it off' was misheard as 'shut her up' during Lindsay Clancy trial.
Defense lawyer accused prosecutors of inappropriate comments during Clancy's emotional courtroom moment.
Judge Sullivan issued a warning against disruptive comments, threatening removal without further notice.

title: Little boy dancing to DJ on Boston Common has hundreds of thousands of new fans
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: 4-year-old Chukwuemeka Ikesinachi-Nwogwugwu gained viral fame for his dance moves on Boston Common, amassing over 200,000 likes.
Chidimma Ikesinachi shared the video, surprised by the positive reaction and happy to spread joy through her son's dancing.
Miss S. Peace's popup DJ show on the Common, aimed at fostering human connection, inspired spontaneous dancing from attendees.

title: Boston wine bar will keep its signature pours, just without the wine
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Barcelona Wine Bar will serve juice and soda instead of wine in traditional porrón pours after license suspension.
Boston's Licensing Board suspended the bar's liquor license for three days due to serving alcohol to underage patrons.
The restaurant updated ID-checking policies and added scanners following violations found during a May inspection.

title: Could Mike Vrabel keep 7 wide receivers on Patriots’ roster?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Mike Vrabel may keep seven wide receivers on the Patriots' roster for the upcoming NFL season.
New additions A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs strengthen a competitive wideout group featuring Kayshon Boutte and Kyle Williams.
Trade rumors surround Kayshon Boutte, while Kyle Williams looks to secure a significant offensive role despite recent struggles.

title: Suffolk DA candidates dispute ethics, transparency, experience at Roxbury debate
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Candidates clashed on ethics, police accountability, and leadership at the Suffolk DA debate in Roxbury.
Kevin Hayden faced criticism over a previous ethics violation; Rachael Rollins resigned after a federal ethics investigation.
Linda Champion emphasized transparency and independence, critiquing Hayden's handling of police body-camera footage.

title: What Boston meteorologists are saying about this weekend’s humidity levels, the potential for pop-up storms
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: Heat and humidity continue in southern New England, with highs near 90°F and heat advisories in effect.
Pop-up thunderstorms are possible Friday and Saturday evenings, with Sunday remaining humid but dry.
Humidity will remain high over the weekend, with dew points in the 60s making conditions feel sticky.
